jobs.prompt: Minimalist, cohesive video game screenshot of 'War Table', a calm world-conquest strategy board game in the spirit of classic Risk: a recognizable world map (the Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia) divided into territories owned by four players. The design combines two things: (1) the palette and discipline of a dark 'night ink' app — deep indigo-navy ground, soft low-saturation territory tints in muted coral, slate blue, pale gold and sage, gold used only for hairline accents and the single active element, one elegant high-contrast serif (like Cormorant Garamond), generous negative space; and (2) the structure of Japanese sumi-e ink linework — coastlines drawn as expressive tapered brush strokes that swell and thin with dry-brush texture at their ends, territory colors applied as soft ink washes that fade at the edges (bokashi), a few sparse calligraphic brush strokes suggesting waves in the ocean, and the zen ensō brush circle as the recurring motif. Exactly ONE mark per territory: a small serif number inside a small brushed ensō circle. No figures, no seals, no fake characters, no scenery clutter. Everything must feel like one cohesive, restrained design system. Wide landscape 16:9 desktop view of the whole board mid-game. At the bottom, a thin gold rule with a small brushed ensō in its center, then a rounded pill segmented control 'Place  Attack  Fortify  End turn' with 'Attack' softly lit, and one small 'Blitz' button. One territory is selected with a brighter brush outline and a single fluid brush-stroke arrow curving to its neighbor. Variant: silver ink on indigo paper. The ground reads like deep indigo-dyed washi paper with the faintest fiber texture; coastlines are brushed in warm silver-ivory ink with confident tapered strokes; territory washes are translucent and bleed softly at the brush edges; ocean has 5-6 sparse calligraphic wave strokes in faint silver. High detail, premium, readable, no watermark, no taglines.
